title: Sunburst motif — basic
subtitle: A six-spoke radiating motif in DK cotton, worked in three rounds
excerpt: Six treble clusters radiate from the centre like spokes on a wheel, giving this 10 cm motif its sunburst shape. Three rounds in a single colour produce a graphic geometric tile; swap the centre round for a contrast colour and the spokes read as rays against a ring border.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1888), radiating-spoke motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet motif section.
heroPrompt: A basic sunburst crochet motif in golden yellow DK cotton on a cream linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Six radiating treble spokes visible from the centre magic ring, 10 cm across, perfectly flat.

chartDefinition.title: Sunburst motif — basic
chartDefinition.caption: The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Six treble-cluster spokes radiate from the centre; chain-2 spaces separate each spoke. Round 3 works a double crochet border into the spoke tips and chain arches.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three trebles worked into the same space and drawn together at the top into one stitch. Forms the spoke tips in this sunburst motif.
The gap created by a length of chain stitches. In this motif the chain-2 and chain-4 spaces form the arches between each sunburst spoke.

content.text: The sunburst motif builds six
treble cluster

spokes from a tight magic ring, then extends each spoke outward across two rounds until the motif reaches 10 cm. The geometry is stable: six spokes divide the round equally, and the chain arches between them hold the shape flat without curling. It works as a stand-alone coaster, as a tile in a throw, or as a centrepiece in a more complex block.
Two colours give a crisper read: work round 1 in a contrast (the spoke centre), rounds 2 and 3 in the main colour (the halo). One colour gives a quieter, more textural result.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of DK-weight cotton in one or two colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins for a flat finish.

content.text: Gauge

Each finished sunburst motif measures 10 cm across at widest point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-block. Work one test motif before starting a project with several — slight tension differences compound across a full blanket.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; equivalent to US "single crochet".
treble cluster (3tr-cl) — three trebles worked into the same space, drawn together at the top. UK; equivalent to US "3dc-cl".
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Do not turn.
Round 1
Form a
magic ring

. Ch 3 (counts as first tr of first cluster). Work 2 more tr into the ring, draw all 3 loops together (first 3tr-cl made). *Ch 2, work 3tr-cl into the ring*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of first cluster to join. Pull tail to close ring. (6 clusters, 6 ch-2 spaces.)
Round 2

Sl st into first ch-2 space. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 2 more tr into same ch-2 sp, draw together (3tr-cl). Ch 4. *Work 3tr-cl into next ch-2 sp. Ch 4.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Sl st to top of first cluster to join. (6 clusters, 6 ch-4 arches.)
Round 3

Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). Dc into top of first cluster. Ch 2. *Work 4dc into next ch-4 arch. Ch 2. Dc into top of next cluster. Ch 2.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Work 4dc into last ch-4 arch. Ch 2. Sl st to first dc to join. (36 dc, 12 ch-2 spaces.)
Chart

The chart reads outward from the magic ring, anti-clockwise. Six cluster spokes show as bold vertical symbols; the ch-4 arches of round 2 expand the spoke spacing; the dc border of round 3 completes the halo.

definition.title: Sunburst motif — basic
definition.caption: Six treble-cluster spokes from the magic ring. Ch-4 arches in round 2; dc border with ch-2 gaps in round 3.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Weave the tail through 3 to 4 stitches on the back of round 3, then back through 2 to 3 stitches in the opposite direction. Trim. Weave in the magic ring tail along the back of round 1. Steam-block by holding a steam iron 2 to 3 cm above the motif for 10 seconds, then leave flat to cool. The chain arches will open up to full width with blocking.
Joining

Join sunburst motifs through the ch-2 spaces on round 3. For a flat grid, whipstitch through the back loops of matching dc pairs with a tapestry needle. The hexagonal spacing of the six spokes means these tiles suit a honeycomb arrangement rather than a square grid. Use the advanced sunburst motif (slug: crochet-sunburst-motif-advanced) for a 14 cm version with a fourth decorative round.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a small amount of mild soap, or machine-wash on a wool cycle. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.
What to try next

The advanced sunburst (crochet-sunburst-motif-advanced) adds a fourth round of shell stitches for a 14 cm tile with more surface texture. The African flower motif (crochet-african-flower-three-colour) uses a similar six-spoke logic but fills the spaces between spokes with petal shapes.
